llm.summary: This is a disclosed website monitoring skill that schedules checks and uses existing Vercel or GA4 credentials only for the monitoring features it describes.

dimensions.detail: The skill reads declared environment variables and selected openclaw.json entries for delegated Vercel/GA4 skills, and its own network checks are constrained to configured watch URLs; this is sensitive but disclosed and proportionate.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is a normal OpenClaw skill install with Node; cron jobs are created only through an explicit schedule --apply command, and the systemd timer is a documented manual fallback.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are scoped to monitoring workflows, include safeguards against inventing URLs or pasting tokens into chat, and do not contain session-hijacking or hidden evaluator instructions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: It writes a local state file for alert deduplication and can create scheduled jobs when requested, which is expected for a monitor and is not hidden or automatic on install.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifacts coherently implement uptime monitoring, scheduled alerts, Vercel polling, and GA4 delegation consistent with the stated Web Observer purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, confirm you want this skill to create scheduled monitoring jobs and store local alert state. If you enable Vercel or GA4, understand that it will read those delegated skills' configured credentials from OpenClaw config and pass them to the matching child skill. Keep raw Vercel log messages disabled unless you are comfortable with application log text being delivered into chat.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Scanner mismatch findings are downgraded: the full artifact includes monitoring behavior and supporting modules for CLI dispatch, diagnostics, credential bridging, and delegated Vercel/GA4 execution.
[AE1] expected: Reading delegated skills' SKILL.md files is used for installed-version and capability checks; it is disclosed and not a remote or hidden payload reference.
[PE3] expected: Credential handling is real but disclosed: selected Vercel/GA4 values are read from existing OpenClaw configuration and passed to the corresponding child skill environment, not printed or written by Web Observer.
[RA2] expected: State files, cron jobs, and the optional systemd timer are persistence mechanisms, but they are expected for scheduled monitoring and require user setup or --apply.
[RA1] unexpected: The cited systemd comment asks the user to edit a SKILL_DIR setting in a copied service file; I did not find self-modification of the skill's code or configuration at runtime.
[LP3] expected: The artifact lacks a stronger formal permission boundary, but SKILL.md explicitly declares the environment variables, files, credentials, network scope, and subprocess delegation behavior.
[EA2] unexpected: The cited instruction not to ask users to paste tokens is a protective credential-handling rule, not evidence of autonomous high-impact action.
